data.narrative:
Hexium is a Seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Charlie Jarrott and Jacob Peterson that has raised $10M+. The nuclear energy sector comp universe includes 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private companies, notably Nano Nuclear Energy, Oklo, X-Energy, Fuse Energy, and Applied Atomics.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable triangulation method here. Using total capital raised ($10M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression yields $25M. This method directly applies to Hexium's current stage and funding profile.

Peer-median valuation could not be reliably applied. While 4 same-sector peers exist in the nuclear energy space, insufficient clustering emerged within narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, similar-tier comparables). The private comp set skews toward later-stage and larger valuations, and constructing a median from fewer than three comparable datapoints within Hexium's cohort would lack analytical rigor.

The triangulated valuation range is $21M–$29M (median $25M), derived from the stage-progression method alone. Key uncertainties stem from the thinness of the comparable peer set at Hexium's early stage, the heterogeneity of technology approaches across nuclear energy startups, and absence of revenue or deployed-capacity data. Validation against post-Seed funding terms and investor appetite in frontier nuclear will be material to range refinement.
